answer: A WARNING is raised when projected 15-minute demand reaches **1,125 kW**—90% of the **1,250 kW** contract capacity—or when next-hour exceedance probability is at least 20%. The 1,125 kW line provides headroom before contract exceedance; normal summer peaks of 1,100–1,180 kW can approach it on hot afternoons. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Demand status tiers] [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Key terms]

Demand above the 1,250 kW contract capacity is billed for each interval: excess demand up to 10% above the contract is charged at 2× the applicable period’s contract price; any excess beyond that is charged at 3×. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Exceedance] [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Contract capacity]

answer: The night-load baseline uses a CUSUM allowance of **k = 0.5** and an alarm threshold of **h = 8 robust sigmas**. It also requires night load to be more than 3 kW above expectation. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Trigger]

It predicts the change from an anchor because the earlier level-target model missed contract-limit exceedances. Tree models cannot extrapolate above values seen during training, and the plant rarely exceeded the 1,250 kW contract then; forecasting an increment lets the model add start-up- or heat-driven load to the current load instead. For 15 minutes–3 hours, the anchor is the last completed interval; day-ahead uses the same time last week. [source: docs/forecasting.md#Load forecasting > Model]

In summer (16 May–15 October), weekday peak hours are 16:00–22:00. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-03_tariff_guide.md#EM-03 Tariff Guide > Time-of-use periods and energy prices > Summer (16 May - 15 October)]

answer:
On a hot weekday afternoon, start the heat-wave pre-cooling response when the next-hour exceedance probability is at least 20% (WARNING) or 50% (ALARM), or when WARNING occurs before 16:00. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Trigger]

Before the 16:00–22:00 peak, have Facilities lower the chilled-water setpoint gradually, keep CH-01 lead, and stage CH-02 early; do not manually start a chiller during the peak. Hold non-essential start-ups, including optional burn-in loading and test runs, and use the required staggered order for essential starts. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 2: pre-cool] [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 3: hold non-essential start-ups]

At WARNING/ALARM, monitor every interval and shed only until projected demand is below the 1,250 kW contract: pause EV charging; delay the next burn-in load; raise chilled-water setpoint by 1°C if pre-cooling margin permits; then lower compressed-air pressure by 0.5 bar. Never shed the server room, molders mid-cycle, or reflow ovens containing boards. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 6: during the peak] [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

Once stable below 1,125 kW, restore in reverse order—pressure, setpoint, burn-in, then EV charging—and do not restore everything simultaneously. Record the trigger, projected demand, actions/times, interval peak, and likely cause in the shift log. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 5: restore] [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 4: record]

Yes. The compressed-air leak was detected on 2025-09-09 at 06:00; it raised night base load by up to 18.1 kW (reported impact: +18 kW around the clock). [data: list_detections]

Inspection procedure (SOP-04): perform an ultrasonic walk-down during a quiet period—ideally at night or Sunday—covering main headers/branches, pneumatic-use areas (especially injection molding), fittings, couplers, hoses, filter/regulator units, drains, blow-off nozzles, the dryer area and compressor room. Tag and record each leak, then isolate/depressurize the affected section, repair it, re-pressurize and recheck. Verify over subsequent nights that compressor night load returns to its earlier baseline; repeat the walk-down if it does not.
